messages.body:
Hi,
Does somebody know how to correct this horrible font in ubuntu 20.04 LTS ?
As long as I can't correct it I use tleap but I would like to use xleap
as recommanded in tutorials,
Sorry if it's not a problem with amber20, I guess it's a problem of
fonts in ubuntu/debian but someone might have any ideas about that ?
Thank you very much

messages.author: Gustaf Olsson
messages.body:
I am sure it is possible, though as far as I found after a quick search, there is no simple way to change the font of applications being forwarded. If the application is gtk based, it seems possible with a little work though I don’t know if xleap is gtk based or native x.
Changing the font of the xterm is simple though changing fonts in applications being forwarded (server-client) seems like a bigger problem. There should likely be some configuration for xleap somewhere defining the font to use.
In any case, the fonts used by XQuartz (what I am using) are not very pretty to begin with.
[cid:
8FC54613-A4DA-42DA-8F92-D9CEF501ADE5.client.lnu.se
][cid:
2EE9A5F9-0F3D-48F4-BD64-3261A5F606AF.client.lnu.se
]
If you are interested in doing a little research I found an informative page here: https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/x-window-system/9780937175149/Chapter05.html
It might provide a good starting point to see if you can find a solution, please do share if you manage to figure something out.
// Gustaf

messages.author: Gustaf Olsson
messages.body:
Yes, works on my end as well. Good one!
Using a combination of xlsfonts, xfd and grep you can pretty much pick a font you like and then just make alias entries in your profile for separate fonts
alias times_leap="xleap -fn '*times-bold-r*150*’"
alias courier_leap="xleap -fn '*times-bold-r*150*’”
and so on.
Glad it worked out!
Best regards
// Gustaf

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Thu, Sep 24, 2020, Gustaf Olsson wrote:
>
>Using a combination of xlsfonts, xfd and grep you can pretty much pick
>a font you like and then just make alias entries in your profile for
>separate fonts
> alias times_leap="xleap -fn '*times-bold-r*150*’"
> alias courier_leap="xleap -fn '*times-bold-r*150*’”
This doesn't work for me, at least on MacOS. The way that does work
(again, for me) is described here:
http://archive.ambermd.org/201707/0353.html
The xleap program is *way,,way,,way* old X-code, written before toolkits
like Qt (etc) were available. Some mouse actions no longer work. But,
a revamping of fonts for modern displays might still be worthwhile. And
if some intrepid soul figures out how to make "deselect" work via the
mouse, that would be great. (There are still some tasks that xleap is
really nice for, but that's probably just because I'm familiar with it,
and not with other drawing programs.)
....dac

messages.author: Gustaf Olsson
messages.body:
Hello David
I have tried this on macOS Mojave 10.14.6 with XQuartz and no other version yet. If you did a “copy-paste” it will fail as the auto format of mail switches the ' character into a ‘ character. This has bitten me several, several times. I also noticed that I had used “times” for both courier and times examples.
alias c_xleap="xleap -fn '*courier-bold-r*150*'"
I used the above, after correcting to a straight apostrophe (“typewriter") instead of the curved “typesetter” (there are likely better terms for both these), producing a side-by-side compartment attached.
[cid:
F73EF753-390C-4E04-B6EE-FCBF80C4B5E2.client.lnu.se
]
I did notice that this makes the selected font the overall default font, as you can se affecting menus in a unintended way. There might be other, less desirable, effects of this solution.
It would be nice with a rewrite of xleap to a more up-to-date cross-platform gui option. Should make it easier to utilise existing and likely add more functionality. Sadly I don’t possess the skill level required to accomplish this.
I have also suffered the “deselect” problem and I have also realised that the mouse emulation of XQuartz does not really work. Using a USB connected PC three button mouse and keyboard instead of the wireless apple alternative or the built in trackpad and keyboard has at leas allowed me to zoom and type in the "edit editor”.
Best regards
// Gustaf

messages.author: Bill Ross
messages.body:
> It would be nice with a rewrite of xleap to a more up-to-date cross-platform gui option.
On the first Amber web site, I was bemused to see that xleap's graphics
library, Xraw (an improvement on Athena widgets) was downloaded at least
10's of thousands of times, way more I'd bet than the cumulative users
of Amber til now (it was free and general-purpose, and Amber itself cost
something, but who knew Xraw'd be so popular). Having traveled to Moscow
in the early 90's to contract Vladimir Romanovski, the author, I feel
uniquely qualified to retract my long-ago suggestion to redo it in Java,
since python is more universal among scientists these days.
If its functions were API'd along the way, the functionality could spread.
Bill
